proposal.title: Define CP/M Aurelia cartridge ROM storage and manufacturing requirements
proposal.reason: Replace the generic media-selection placeholder with one explicitly bounded, image-specific supplied ROM set and matching cartridge acceptance requirements. Prefer qualified AION mask ROM for stable production and separately qualified purchased EPROMs for development/corrections. Preserve existing composition quantities, dates and software ownership. Capacity and chip population remain open until the accepted image and physical implementation are defined. These are manufacturing-definition requirements, not completed qualification or a released unit-cost estimate.

requirements.description: Logix supplies this complete assembly or kit; constituent suppliers remain subject to qualification. Keep this BOM element combined.

after.name: CP/M Aurelia — programmed ROM storage set
after.description: One complete, image-specific set of packaged ROM devices for the CP/M Aurelia cartridge. The carrier PCB, connector, enclosure and software delivery items are supplied separately.

requirements.description: Keep this BOM element as one complete supplied storage set. Release its internal ROM-device population and image-specific drawing; quantity one means one set, not one chip.

Before production costing is treated as released, approve installed capacity, image allocation, ROM technology, density/count, package/pinout, electrical timing, supply/current limits and test operations. Unselected values remain open; do not substitute invented measurements.

Qualify the production mask-ROM route and any EPROM alternative separately, including image verification and matched cartridge/host operation. An existing recipe or software launch does not establish this part-specific qualification.

chapters.description: Logix supplies one combined storage set containing the packaged ROM devices programmed or masked for {software_image}. AION Labs is the intended manufacturer of production mask-ROM chips under {rom_recipe}; Logix remains the set supplier and integration authority. The recipe does not by itself qualify this density, image, speed or package. Exclude the separately supplied carrier PCB, connector, sockets, decoding/buffering, enclosure, label, hardware packout, software licence and documentation. No writable RAM is included.

The installed storage capacity, used image bytes, identification/checksum allocation and reserved space must be fixed from the accepted linked image. No ROM capacity or chip count is established by the host RAM requirement. Store the integrated CP/M, platform extensions and shared TUI release; motherboard boot/monitor ROM and the Business Tools application cartridge are outside this set.

Use mask ROM for stable production images after order-specific qualification. Separately qualified purchased EPROMs may serve development and small correction batches; do not assume that AION manufactures EPROMs or that the replacement is pin-compatible. EEPROM is not the default. Keep the mask-ROM baseline and EPROM alternative separate in the production drawing and costing. Replacement cartridges provide the update path; no in-system erase/program capability is implied.

The storage interface is {interface_width_bits} bits wide, using the qualified Aurelia bank-selection mechanism. Freeze bytes per device, device width, device count and bank addressing without assuming that the CPU address-space size limits total banked storage. Release numeric supply rails and tolerances, access/output-enable/disable timing, loading, active and standby current, and the qualified host wait-state profile. Direct execution does not imply zero-wait operation. Specify the exact packaged-device pinout, temperature grade, marking and mounting requirements. Socket or solder details, board area, decoupling and connector protection belong to the carrier assembly and must fit its released envelope.

chapters.chapter_name: Image installation, test and revision control
chapters.description: Freeze image revision, byte count, bank/lane files, checksum algorithm and expected verification values before mask generation or EPROM programming. Require full-image verification, electrical testing under the released conditions, lot traceability and a matched cartridge boot/function test. The EPROM route needs specified programming voltage, pulse algorithm, verification, erasure/rework limits and cycle time; these are not assumed to match the host supply. A software revision requires assessed new masks or reprogramming, replacement stock and obsolete-stock handling.

For internal mask-ROM production, establish density-specific die area, usable dies per wafer, wafer route, probe/test flow and package before calculating cost. Cost estimates must state wafer/probe and assembly/final-test yield assumptions, mask/setup allocation, lot size, handling and test labour, scrap and rework. For purchased EPROMs use the qualified device quote plus programming and verification operations. Keep prices, changing yields, production volumes and amortisation assumptions in calculation evidence; do not add carrier, enclosure or software costs again.

before.name: CP/M 1.4-derived / Platform Extensions 1.0 (Aurelia edition) — ROM cartridge
before.description: CP/M 1.4-derived / Platform Extensions 1.0 (Aurelia edition) — ROM cartridge

assembly_requirements.description: Freeze actual image size and storage technology; do not assume EEPROM by default.
For XIP choose wide ROM or explicit width adapter/wait states.

DRI supplies the accepted integrated CP/M/TUI release image. Logix freezes cartridge electronics, ROM capacity and electrical timing, then verifies the production image and revision. AION Labs manufactures qualified ROM chips to Logix requirements; capacity, masks/programming, checksum verification and patch/replacement procedure require explicit acceptance.

after.description: CP/M 1.4-derived / Platform Extensions 1.0 (Aurelia edition) — ROM cartridge

assembly_requirements.description: Use the image-specific ROM storage-set definition in this cartridge BOM. Freeze its actual image allocation and qualified population; mask ROM is the stable-production preference and a separately qualified EPROM route is an alternative. Do not default to EEPROM.
Qualify the 8-bit banked-ROM path, cartridge identification, bank selection, timing and wait states with the selected ROM population.

The storage set covers packaged ROM devices only. Release carrier PCB, connector, sockets or solder mounting, decoding/buffering, decoupling and mechanical fit in the separate carrier set; enclosure, label and packout remain separate. Do not duplicate these constituents in the storage cost.

Verify the accepted image revision, bank/lane mapping, checksum, electrical limits and successful boot/function on each qualified host. Control mask/programming revisions, replacement stock and patch/replacement procedures together.

DRI supplies the accepted integrated CP/M/TUI release image. Logix freezes the physical cartridge and AION Labs manufactures qualified production ROM chips to the released capacity, image, timing and package contract. Motherboard ROM and Business Tools remain separate.
